TITLE:
Cosmic Quest: Astrology Explorer – Astronomy + Indian Astrology Edutainment Game
 
INSTRUCTIONS TO THE AI TOOL:
You are to design, develop, and assemble a complete mobile game app called Cosmic Quest: Astrology Explorer. The goal is to create a fun-learning app for students and parents who do not know technical astrology terms. Use the Game Design Document provided below to build the full app, including UI, animations, mini-games, screens, and logic.
 
📌 Build This App Exactly As Described Below
APP PURPOSE
Create a story-based educational adventure game that teaches:
•	Basic astronomy
•	Basic Indian astrology (Jyotish)
In simple, kid-friendly language, without technical terms.
The user becomes a Sky Detective who travels through planets, zodiac realms, and nakshatra villages to restore the broken Cosmic Clock.
 
📌 CORE FEATURES TO BUILD
1. Sky Playground (Astronomy World)
•	Drag planets → build solar system
•	Rotate Earth → show day/night
•	Move Earth around Sun → show seasons
•	Eclipse alignment simulator
•	Connect-the-stars constellation mini-game
 
2. Zodiac Realms (12 Rashi Worlds)
For each of the 12 zodiac signs:
•	Guardian character
•	Constellation drawing
•	Element animation
•	Story narration
•	Mini-quests (puzzles, emotion sorting, trait matching)
 
3. Planet Worlds (9 Graha Personalities)
Create interactive worlds for:
Surya, Chandra, Mangal, Budh, Guru, Shukra, Shani, Rahu, Ketu.
Each world must include:
•	Character avatar
•	Simple metaphorical traits
•	Orbit visual
•	Planet challenge mini-game
 
4. Nakshatra Village (27 Levels)
•	27 star clusters
•	Each village = star mascot + symbol + simple meaning
•	Moon alignment puzzles
•	Region categories: Deva / Manushya / Rakshasa
 
5. Birth Sky Map Generator
Input:
•	Birth date
•	Birth time
•	Birth place (location API)
Output (non-technical):
•	Sun Character
•	Moon Emotion Animal
•	Lagna (Action Style)
•	Planet helper strengths (1–10)
•	Lucky element
•	Balance tips
NO predictions. Only simple learning summaries.
 
6. Cosmic Clock Hub
•	Shows player progress
•	Stores collected Cosmic Shards
•	Unlocks next world
 
7. Rewards & Progression
•	Cosmic Shards
•	Badges
•	Certificates
•	Unlockable outfits for characters
 
8. Parent Mode
•	Simple horoscope summary
•	Daily “Sky Fact”
•	Track child learning
•	No jargon
 
📌 UI & ART STYLE REQUIREMENTS
•	Cartoon, colourful, Indian-spiritual + space-fantasy theme
•	Soft gradients, glowing stars, friendly mascots
•	Minimal text, maximum icons
•	Voice narration for kids
•	Visually guided learning
 
📌 TECH REQUIREMENTS
•	Platform: Mobile (Android + iOS)
•	Game engine: Unity / Godot / Flutter Game Toolkit
•	Local database for offline use
•	Birth place lookup using offline city DB or Google Maps
•	Save progress locally + cloud sync
•	Child-safe (no ads)

•	Orbit Builder
•	Star Line Connect
•	Rotation-Revolution Race
•	Eclipse Maker
Zodiac:
•	Element Matching
•	Constellation Finder
•	Personality Trait Puzzle
Nakshatra:
•	Star Pattern Puzzle
•	Moon Path Tracker
Astrology concepts:
•	Planet Friendship Matching
•	Life House Sorting (“Rooms of Life”)
 
📌 AUDIO REQUIREMENTS
•	Peaceful ambient music
•	Mythological Indian tones for zodiac realms
•	Cute mascot voice lines
•	Reward jingles
 
📌 FINAL DELIVERABLE
Build a fully functional app with:
•	All screens
•	All worlds
•	All animations
•	All mini-games
•	Birth Sky Map engine
•	Parent Mode
•	Clean UI

**Developing the Framework**

Okay, I'm now focusing on the initial framework for Cosmic Quest. The application will center on a React web app with the name "Cosmic Quest: Astrology Explorer". My primary goal is an edutainment game, blending astronomy and Jyotish, with features that cater to both beginners and advanced users. I'm prioritizing user experience and clear, accessible design elements.


**Expanding Core Features**

I've just added several key features and features, including Sky Playground, Zodiac Realms, Planet Worlds, Nakshatra Village, Birth Sky Map and Cosmic Clock Hub. I'm focusing on React 18+, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS.

I'm now focusing on core UI components like the navbar, footer, and basic buttons and cards. These will be shared throughout the application for consistency. For data, I'll use simplified solar system positions initially, and a simplified astrology library for calculating Rashi and Graha positions. This will allow me to prioritize user understanding and engagement with the application.

I've decided to incorporate audio controls, even though I can't bundle MP3s due to the restrictions. Instead of actual sound, I'll simulate the UI controls for volume and mute. The UI elements will give the impression of audio, even if no sound is generated. Similarly, for images, I'll use SVG placeholders to maintain a consistent cartoon aesthetic for planets, enhancing the visual experience. I'm leveraging `picsum` as suggested, but will make strategic use of SVG placeholders to suit the project's visual direction.
